board: Iterate the Loehr HR-group landing page (JEV-audit-driven)

phases.label: Discover
phases.question: What is the real human problem?

phases.label: Develop
phases.question: What could the answer look like?

phases.label: Deliver
phases.question: What ships, and how is it built?

cards.title: Where did the JEV audit leave the page, honestly?
cards.body: JEV-AUDIT.md: web.market FINAL 0.747 (baseline 0.649), no BLOCK at any point, but the 0.9 mean was never reached. Strongest fit items: boring_reliable_job 0.96, rulebook_accountability 0.88. Weakest: diagnostic_wedge (0.17→0.69 after the r4 rewrite), named_pain_lead (0.46→0.73). The iteration target is those two, not a redesign.

cards.title: Which sections already carry evidence the buyer trusts?
cards.body: Live page audit: #hero leads with the named pain ("Your renewal just jumped 27% and nobody can show you what the service fee actually buys"); #operator gives James Loehr — 18 years running operations, largest 37 locations / ~550 employees; #pricing shows the fee in writing plus market context (SHRM Executive Network $3,995/yr, Hacking HR $2,000, Mile High SHRM cap 12 — same cap). These are the credibility spine; the iteration must not dilute them.

cards.title: Who is the reader the audit could not score well — and why?
cards.body: JEV-AUDIT.md website.buyer: mean 0.634 on best-fit section packets, ~0.40 full page. Structural ceiling documented: ~11 rubric questions (vert_healthcare_regulated, typ_free_kit, typ_paid_review, design_visual_evidence…) score the RIG AI-intake product shape — a membership group can score ≤0.1 on them regardless of copy. Doctrine applied: split the bimodal distribution, never average it away. The page should serve the real buyer (Denver HR leader), not chase the mismatched questions.

cards.title: What do the demand-thread pain numbers say?
cards.body: #group / #members carry pain numbers that are JEV scores from a September 2026 sweep of HR-leader demand threads on Reddit (quotes and sources in the research file): pain 6.0 — the solo HR lead paying $1,300/month for tools and getting no human; pain 6.90 — the price jack gets read out loud in the room before the vendor writes it into your renewal. Language rule from the audit: named pain first, product language never.

cards.title: HMW lift named_pain_lead (0.73) to top-of-page strength?
cards.body: From c1 + c4. The hero already opens on the renewal shock; the fix is named-pain precision: one sentence a Denver HR leader says verbatim ("nobody can show you what the service fee actually buys"), kept above the fold in #hero, with the CTA "Apply for the Denver room — 12 seats" directly under it. Target: named_pain_lead ≥ 0.9 on re-run.

cards.title: HMW hold diagnostic_wedge (0.69) without sales pressure?
cards.body: From c2. The wedge is the Guest offer in #pricing/#offers: $0, one diagnostic session a year, bring one document, leave with the room's written read on it — yours to keep whether or not you apply. It must read as the room already working for you, not a lead magnet. No "book a demo" energy.

cards.title: HMW let the pricing page carry the qualifying burden?
cards.body: From c2 + c3. Targeting carries the data burden: #pricing already prices under national networks and inside the local band, caps at 12, bans vendors (including as guests), and prints the fee sheet before the first conversation. The iteration should make "who this is NOT for" a visible line so the wrong applicants self-select out — the structural ceiling stays disclosed, not papered over.

cards.title: HMW close the accessible-apply-form gap on #book?
cards.body: JEV-AUDIT.md ui.design: clarity 0.98, mobile_considered 0.93, primary_action_obvious 0.83, accessible 0.75 — the audit's weakest ui item. The #book form (Name, Work email, Company, What would you put on the table?) needs real labels, error states, contrast that survives the no-pure-#000/#FFF rule, and 44px tap targets. Target: accessible ≥ 0.9 on re-run.

cards.title: Variant A — #hero named-pain spine rewrite
cards.body: Keep the hero photo plate and the "run by an operator, not an association" line; rewrite the lede so the named pain is the first full sentence and the fee-sheet promise is the second. CTA unchanged: "Apply for the Denver room — 12 seats · 30-minute conversation first. No employee data needed." Risk: over-tilting to pain reads alarmist — the no-BLOCK calm from the audit must survive.

cards.title: Variant B — #sequence year-in-the-room timeline
cards.body: "Monthly. Quarterly. Renewal season. Year two." rendered as a four-stop timeline card set — this is the boring_reliable_job 0.96 evidence made visible: the room keeps a rhythm that outlasts the renewal cycle. Mono data labels overline each stop; one concrete meeting cadence per stop.

cards.title: Variant C — #members bring/take ledger with pain numbers
cards.body: "What Members Bring. What Members Take." as a two-column CARD ledger, each row footnoted with the JEV pain score and its source note (September 2026 Reddit sweep, quotes in the research file): pain 6.0 tools-with-no-human, pain 6.90 renewal price jack. Real numbers with provenance, never unattributed stats.

cards.title: Variant D — #pricing fee-sheet decode table
cards.body: Solo seat, Company pack (3 seats, one org, different functions, $6,600/year), Guest diagnostic ($0 · one session) as a three-row comparison, with the verified 2026-09-30 market context as a TRUST STRIP (max 5 stats): SHRM $3,995 · Hacking HR $2,000 · Mile High SHRM cap 12 · this room under the national band · monthly seat = leave any month. Deviation +5 from the system table component — outside the |d| ≤ 3 budget, flagged for human review before shipping.

cards.title: Dev handoff — #hero + #sequence spine (Variants A, B)
cards.body: Ship the named-pain hero and the year-in-the-room timeline. Tokens: light theme (--void #FAF7F2, --cream #F5F0E8, --gold #B8860B, --ink #14110D). Components: OVERLINE, DISPLAY H1 (Cormorant 300, max 2 gold ems), LEDE max 55ch, BUTTON PRIMARY. Acceptance: named_pain_lead ≥ 0.9 and boring_reliable_job held ≥ 0.9 on JEV re-run; mobile_considered ≥ 0.9 at 390px.

cards.title: Dev handoff — accessible #book apply form (c8)
cards.body: Form fields Name, Work email, Company, "What would you put on the table?" — explicit <label>s, inline error states, focus rings in --gold, contrast ≥ 4.5:1 within the token palette, tap targets ≥ 44px, submit "Apply for a seat" with the honest note ("This form opens the 30-minute conversation…"). Acceptance: ui accessible ≥ 0.9 on JEV re-run; no pure #000/#FFF anywhere.

cards.title: Dev handoff — #pricing clarity block (Variant D, flagged)
cards.body: Fee-sheet decode table + TRUST STRIP of verified market context (dates on every number — "Market context, verified 2026-09-30"). Deviation +5 is outside the |d| ≤ 3 budget: human review required before this block ships. If review rejects the custom table, fall back to standard CARD rows with identical copy.

cards.title: Dev handoff — this board exported as a coding bundle
cards.body: The loop closes here: Export dev handoff renders rig-dev-handoff.json (cards, phase, links, deviation scores, token set) + rig-ai-coding-prompts.md (board-level prompt then per-card prompts) into the side panel. A coding agent consumes the bundle directly; the Stitch mockups in the Mockups tab (export handoff modal, mobile canvas 390px) are the visual contract for the same surfaces.
